lines: The golem did good work last night. Still, I keep the blades sharp.
I once polished rust off a sword and found three old mistakes underneath.
Some nights, the grindstone sounds like <pulse>preparation</pulse> instead of work.
There is a story from the grindstone, but it sounds smaller unless you were standing there.
Once a sword came back chipped, muddy, and carried like a thank you.
A young guard asked for the largest blade and learned about arm strength instead.
During one raid, the grindstone worked until sunrise and nobody complained about the noise.
I once found a nick that matched a story the owner did not want to tell.
A trader tried to sell me a heroic dagger with a loose handle. Short heroism.
The first axe I balanced properly felt like it had decided to behave.
A golem stood outside after battle while I repaired tools of louder courage.
There was a spear that survived three owners and one very bad door.
A child asked if swords sleep. I said only when people let them.
I once quenched a blade as the bell rang and nearly cooled my heart with it.
A cracked sword taught its owner to carry a shield with more respect.
The old grindstone has heard more fear than boasting, whatever people claim.
One morning every weapon was clean and the village felt almost too quiet.
A blade I made once came back unused after a long trip. Best review I got.
I repaired a dagger so small the owner called it discreet. I called it nervous.
